messages:
PagerBot: INCIDENT_1526 triggered by 95% packet retransmits on ib0 in eu-west-1. Paging oncall: @Sanjay :rotating_light:
Sanjay (oncall): on it — starting triage. seeing lots of IB retransmit counters incrementing on 10.22.3.* nodes. CUDA watchdog resets reported on serve-rt containers.
Ashley (eng-runtime): confirmed multiple serving containers crashed with `CUDA_ERROR_DEVICE_RESET` and `segfault` right after IB link flaps. Logs: ```kernel: mlx5_core 0000:83:00.0: mlx5_ib: port 1 got error: QP flush due to port state change```.
Jenny (sre): grabbing infra view + network fabric metrics. consequences: increased 5xx in routed requests and long tail for model-1 (v3).
Mike (infra): Found ECMP churn on ToR -> spine causing microloops. I see repeated BGP nexthop changes every ~30s for prefixes that host RDMA nodes. suspect route flapping triggers IB link recalcs.
Ashley (eng-runtime): runtime observed heavy KV cache misses during those intervals, then containers OOM during recovery attempts (memory spike on rebuild). stack traces show rapid re-allocation of KV caches during reconnect.
Sanjay (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain most-affected nodes, 2) re-route traffic away from that rack, 3) failover to CPU-backed serving as graceful fallback for critical customers, 4) apply temporary ECMP pinning i.e., disable equal-cost multipath on affected ToRs.
Mike (infra): executing `kubectl cordon node-10.22.3.14 && kubectl drain node-10.22.3.14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` now. pulling BGP config diff, applying static ecmp policy patch to pin to single nexthop for the affected prefixes (will do one ToR at a time).
PagerBot: oncall escalation: SLO alert triggered — model-1 tail latency > 5s for 12% of requests. Severity: SEV2.
CS-Bot: Notifying customers in eu-west-1 with degraded perf tag. Draft message sent to #status-drafts.
Jenny (sre): adding kernel BPF drop rule to limit retransmit storms while infra patches routes: `bpftool prog load` + small XDP drop on offending NIC to shed bad traffic.
Ashley (eng-runtime): pushed a canary rollback to model-1 config to reduce batch_size from 64 -> 8 to lower memory pressure. Also enabling prefix-KV persistence to avoid full rebuilds.
Sanjay (oncall): after drains, observed fewer CUDA resets but a few nodes still show `mlx5_core` errors and container restarts. Looks like firmware mismatch on one NIC model (8800-something) — Mike to handle.
Mike (infra): spinning firmware rollback and scheduling a patch window. For immediate live mitigation I enabled `MLX5_ENHANCED_MULTIPATH=0` on affected hosts and lowered MTU from 4096 -> 1500 on the host to avoid large packet reassembly issues.
Ashley (eng-runtime): we rolled traffic onto dedicated non-shared NICs for serving pods (node-affinity change). Traffic injection tests look green. Observed 95th latency back to baseline for canary traffic.
Sanjay (oncall): customer impact summary so far: ~8% of total requests in eu-west saw errors (502/503) over 18 minutes, key customers A and C experienced higher error rates — CS is drafting outbound. No data exfiltration or persistent data loss identified.
CS-Bot: sent preliminary notice to customers A and C. CS will escalate contract SLAs for impacted accounts.
Jenny (sre): collecting post-incident artifacts: dmesg, `/var/log/syslog`, `/var/log/serve-rt/*.log`, `nstat` snapshots, ibstat/ibv_devinfo, and `kubectl describe pod` for restarting containers. Archiving to incident bucket: s3://incidents/1903007890/.
PagerBot: Added runbook tag: rdma-pktstorms -> follow rdma/ib fabric checklist and runtime OOM fallout steps.
Ashley (eng-runtime): follow-up actions: 1) add guardrail in runtime to backoff KV rebuild concurrency when RDMA flaps detected, 2) implement adaptive batch-size throttle when CUDA memory pressure spikes, 3) produce eval to validate CPU fallback for latency-sensitive customers.
Sanjay (oncall): handing off to Jenny for 8:00 followup rota. @Jenny you're pager for postmortem. I'll remain reachable for rollout decisions. :white_check_mark:
Jenny (sre): ack taking over. compiling timeline and RCA notes. Initial hypothesis: ECMP/BGP churn induced packet storms -> IB link state transitions -> RDMA QP flushes -> runtime KV rebuild + memory surge -> CUDA watchdog resets -> container restarts -> request errors.
Mike (infra): we'll coordinate firmware validation and a staged MTU/ECMP config change across eu-west racks. ETA for full mitigation ~6 hours.
Ashley (eng-runtime): adding a temporary traffic-routing rule in Console to route eu-west pre-prod traffic to other regions for critical customers while infra remediates.
PagerBot: SEV2 downgraded to SEV3 at 1903011200 per SRE lead after mitigations show stable metrics.
Jenny (sre): last check: error rate back to baseline, some nodes still under observation. I'll open a postmortem ticket and link artifacts. thanks everyone — great coordination. :pray:
